title: Completed org-space case — two-car garage (Ada Lovelace sample)
source: backend/samples + tests/test_pdf_build.py garage deliverable, completed with six Brain layers
notes: Not a bedroom. Shell preserved. No invented footage. Paint optional. Answers Ryan's five bake-off questions from layers + PDF.

lead.name: Ada Lovelace
lead.biggest_challenge: Can't park both cars and still find tools or the kids' sports bags.
lead.goals: Park nightly, find gear in under a minute, less visual noise.
lead.must_stay: Existing workbench, kids' bikes, lawn mower
lead.daily_improvement: Park both cars after school pickup, drop sports bags by the door, grab tools without stepping over piles.

deliverable.intro: A garage that is easy to park in and easy to find things — same walls and windows, a calmer system.
needs: A landing zone by the door for sports bags

zones.title: Parking Zone
zones.desc: Keep the existing stall clear. No new walls.

zones.title: Storage Zone
zones.desc: Bins and wall-mounted shelves on the existing wall.

zones.title: Circulation Zone
zones.desc: Keep the walk path your photo already shows.

zones.title: Workbench
zones.desc: Tools in labeled bins on the workbench you already own.

zones.title: Door Drop
zones.desc: Hooks and a basket for daily in-and-out.

deliverable.wall_color_note: Optional — consider if it helps the goal.
strategy: Leave a path to the car
action_plan: Mount shelves on the existing wall
deliverable.notes: Windows and room proportions stay ~95% true to your photo. We do not invent dimensions. Paint is optional — consider it only if it helps your goal.
deliverable.summary: Organize the garage you already have: stall stays a destination, tools and sports get labeled homes on existing walls.

observation.space_seen: Two-car garage photographed as used today: floor is a dump, tools mixed with sports bags, existing workbench still in place, bikes and mower share the stall.
current_state: Tools and sports gear share one pile
No landing zone at the door
evidence: Must keep: existing workbench, kids' bikes, lawn mower.
Daily goal: park both cars after school pickup and find gear fast.
Photo is the source of truth for the shell. No invented footage.

human_need.routine: After-school pickup: park both cars, drop sports bags at the door, grab a tool without stepping over piles, leave a clear stall overnight.
jobs_to_be_done: Find a sports bag in under a minute
human_need.pain: Can't park both cars and still find tools or the kids' sports bags.

known_from_photo: Keep the existing parking stall as a destination, not a dump.
Use the walls and door path the photo already shows.
Workbench stays where it already sits.
unknowns: Exact footage, window counts, and opening sizes were not measured — we do not invent them.

recommendation.system: Five zones on the existing shell: stall, wall storage, circulation, workbench bins, door drop.

zones.title: Parking Zone
zones.why: Stall stays empty so both cars fit the path the photo already shows.

zones.title: Storage Zone
zones.why: Matching bins and two wall shelves get tools off the floor.

zones.title: Circulation Zone
zones.why: The walk path in the photo stays the walk path.

zones.title: Workbench
zones.why: Keep the bench they already own; only add labeled bins.

zones.title: Door Drop
zones.why: Hooks + basket catch sports bags at the daily entry.

recommendation.why_it_should_work: The routine is park → drop bags → find a tool. Zoning the stall, the door, and the existing bench removes the pile that blocks all three, without changing walls or windows.

fit.note: Two wall shelves, peg hooks, and lidded bins mount on the existing wall and sit on the workbench they already own. No new walls.

flow.note: Door drop → circulation → stall. Floor mat marks the parking destination; bags never land in the stall.

budget_band.note: Kit totals $227, inside the stated $100 – $300 band.

possession_respect.note: Workbench stays. Bikes hang or stand on the existing wall path. Mower parks beside the stall, not in it.

conflicts: Mower vs stall: mower must live on the side wall, not in a parking bay.
assumptions: Existing walls can take light shelving and peg hooks.
Customer will confirm retail prices before buying.

customer_instruction.start_here: Clear the stall and the door path first — nothing stays on the floor overnight.
do_this_week: Mount two shelves on the existing wall
Park tools in labeled lidded bins on the workbench
Hang door-drop hooks and the sports basket
do_not: Do not add walls, windows, or doors.
Paint is optional — skip it unless it helps the goal.
customer_instruction.weekly_reset: Return tools to labeled bins, hang bags on the door hooks, roll the mower to the side wall, wipe the workbench.
